info.title: The Fridge Door API
info.summary: Plan a week of meals and get a consolidated grocery list.

get.description: The process is running. Does not touch the database.

The configuration is complete and the database has the tables,
columns and permissions this application needs.

Configuration first: a deployment missing a required secret can reach
its database and serve reads, then fail on the first sign-in. That
happened to preview deployments, which had the database URL but not the
rate-limit key; this makes it visible to anyone who checks.

The probes are read-only, need no session or access to migration
history, and accept compatible additive schema changes. PostgreSQL
queries and lock waits have transaction-local timeouts.

post.description:
Start a guest session: a real account with no email or password.

The app calls this when a request comes back 401, so a first visit
lands straight in a working planner, with sample meals if it asks for
them. A caller who is already signed in gets their own account back
(200) rather than a second one.

Create an account. A guest becomes the account, keeping their data.

The response carries the account's recovery code, shown once: the only
way back in if the password is forgotten.

Set a new password with the email and recovery code, and sign in.

Ends every other session of the account, and replaces the recovery code
(each works once): the response carries the new one. The refusal is the
same whether the email or the code is wrong, 401 invalid-credentials,
throttled with login.
Sign in with an email and password. Always issues a new session.
End this session. Succeeds even if it had already ended.

get.description:
Everything that is yours, as a JSON file to download: the account,
every meal with its ingredients, and every planned day.

post.description:
A new recovery code, confirmed with the password; the old one stops
working. For a code that was lost, or never made.

delete.description:
Delete the account and everything in it, for good, and sign out.

An account with a login confirms with its password; a wrong one is a
401 invalid-credentials, throttled with login. A guest needs nothing.

get.description:
Everything needed to render the app for one week, in one response.

Deliberately one endpoint rather than four. The Streamlit version issued
a separate query per section on every interaction, which cost nothing
against a local SQLite file and roughly a second against a database
across a network. Clients fetch this once and hold it.
Every meal, each with its ingredients.

schema.title: Response List Meals Api Meals Get

post.description: Create a meal. Duplicate names are rejected with 409.

patch.description: Rename a meal or change its base serving size.

delete.description: Delete a meal, its ingredient links, and its day assignments.

post.description: Create a meal and its ingredients from a built-in template.
Attach an ingredient, creating it if the name is new.

patch.description: Overwrite the quantity and unit of one ingredient on a meal.

delete.description: Detach an ingredient from a meal, leaving the ingredient itself.

get.description: The meals assigned to each day of the week containing `week`.

put.description: Assign several days at once, in a single transaction.

post.description:
Carry the previous week's assignments onto this one.

Days unassigned in the source are skipped rather than clearing the
target, so copying never destroys work already done here.

get.description: Consolidated shopping list for the week containing `week`.

Account.title: Account
Account.description:
Who is signed in. No id: the client never needs it, and a numeric id
would tell anyone signing up roughly how many accounts exist.

AccountDeletion.title: AccountDeletion
AccountDeletion.description:
Confirmation for deleting an account. An account with a login sends
its password; a guest, who has none, sends nothing.

AccountExport.title: AccountExport
AccountExport.description:
Everything the app holds that is the caller's own, in a form a person
can read and another program can import: names rather than internal
ids, which mean nothing outside this database.

Not included, because they are not content: the password hash, session
tokens, and throttle records, which are keyed hashes of an email or
network and expire on their own.

AppState.title: AppState
AppState.description:
Everything the UI needs for one week, in a single response.

The point of this endpoint is latency: the Streamlit version issued a
separate query per section on every interaction, which is unnoticeable
against a local file and painful across a network. One request, one
round trip.

Credentials.title: Credentials
Credentials.description:
An email and password, for signup and login.

The bounds here only keep request bodies sane. The rules a password must
meet at signup are checked in app/security.py, which can say exactly
what is wrong, rather than with a generic validation error.

DayAssignment.title: DayAssignment
DayAssignment.description: A day as the API returns it: every field present.

DayAssignmentWrite.title: DayAssignmentWrite
DayAssignmentWrite.description:
A day as a client sends it: strict about unknown fields, lenient about
omitted ones, which default to a cleared day.

DayOfWeek.title: DayOfWeek
DayOfWeek.description:
The seven days. Declaration order is display order, so `list(DayOfWeek)`
is the single source of truth for "Monday first".

GroceryLine.title: GroceryLine
GroceryLine.description: One shopping line. qty stays numeric so clients can sort or price it.

GuestStart.title: GuestStart
GuestStart.description:
Optional: ask for sample meals, planned in the week containing this
date (the browser's own week, since the server cannot know its zone).

IngredientAmount.title: IngredientAmount
IngredientAmount.description: One ingredient attached to a meal, with how much of it.

MealRead.title: MealRead
MealRead.description: A meal and everything needed to render it.

MealUpdate.title: MealUpdate
MealUpdate.description: Same fields as creation; every one is required on update.

Recovery.title: Recovery
Recovery.description: A forgotten password replaced, proven with the recovery code.

RecoveryCode.title: RecoveryCode
RecoveryCode.description: A new recovery code; the one before it no longer works.

SignedUp.title: SignedUp
SignedUp.description:
The account just signed up to, or recovered, with its new recovery
code. The code is in this one response and nowhere else, not even the
database (which keeps a hash): the client must show it to be saved.

Problem.description: The body of every error response.
